class: Any guard - a database CHECK, a type check, a wording check, a privilege check, or a test that is meant to detect a reopened hole - written as a list of FORBIDDEN things (named bad shapes, named bad types, bad words, bad privilege paths) lets through everything its author did not imagine; the guard must state what IS allowed (exact key sets, a closed type per slot, a closed name list) and refuse the rest, and its test must enumerate the allowed shape against every other type, generated rather than hand-listed. This is the wider shape of privilege-guard-as-denylist, advice-wording-denylist-per-module, secret-filter-by-key-name and jsonpath-check-lax-mode-unwraps-arrays.
mechanism: On 2026-10-09 the same shape appeared twice in one session after the 2026-10-08 handover had already named the lesson ('every guard built as a list of bad things failed review; every fix that held was structural'): W-061 round 2's jsonpath CHECK refused 13 named bad shapes (an Opus review then stored arrays and prices in leg slots, 6 of 6 reproduced), and W-066's slot-detection test forbade 4 named open slot types (the final Tier A review switched a slot to Quoted - mutation M17 - and every test stayed green).

first_seen.evidence: W-061: orchestrator throwaway pytest on ofo_test as ofo_app, 6 of 6 'DID NOT RAISE'; W-066: final review mutation M17 survived (domain 618 + 16, app 43 green); after the allow-list rewrite (bfd35e1) the verifier's Quoted mutant gave 7 failed.

fix: Instance fixes: W-061 round 3 positive plpgsql walker (generated matrix); W-066 round 4 slot allow-list. Class mechanism (learning L2, second occurrence): a standing quality-bar line in docs/process/builder-brief.md - 'A guard is an allow-list, never a list of forbidden things ... A guard written as refuse X, Y, Z fails review' - which every builder brief and reviewer checklist carries.

detection.note: The brief line is a review gate, not an automated check; no test can recognise a deny-list guard in general. Measure: count of review findings of this shape per week in the registry occurrences; a third occurrence after the brief line names a stronger mechanism (e.g. a reviewer-checklist item that check_brief.py requires in every Tier A brief).

occurrences.evidence: mutation M17 (slot switched to Quoted) survived
